Quick economics notes (short answers so Chloe can paste into MAP):

- Tokens per conversation: our conservative avg for the PulseMed use-case (triage -> follow-up) is ~420 tokens/request (prompt+response). 90th percentile ~1,200 tokens.
- Tokens accounting: we count both prompt+generation tokens. Tool calls (structured data fetches) add their own prompt/response tokens; include them in per-flow totals.
- Prefix-cache hit (40%): means 40% of requests reuse a cached KV cache/prefix (e.g., standard prompts or user metadata) saving full recomputation for the decoder attention constant factors. Practically, this looks like ~18-25% cost reduction on per-token billable compute in our hosted profiles given typical model/kernel mix.
- Batching: the hosted plan supports continuous batching. Our MAP assumptions to date have used a mixed-mode: baseline no-batch unit (for latency-sensitive endpoints) + opportunistic batching for background/async jobs. When batching is applied aggressively to interactive flows you typically see 10–20% additional per-token throughput improvements but median latency can increase ~40–120 ms depending on batch window (default 20–50 ms).

Worked example (numbers to drop into MAP sheet):
- 1k requests/day at avg 420 tokens -> 420k tokens/day.
- With no cache, baseline cost X; with 40% cache hit you can expect ~0.82*baseline token cost (approx).

I attached a brief note (unit_econ_notes.pdf) with the formulas if they want to tweak hit-rate or batching windows.

— Ben

Adding the infra caveats Chloe should surface to Samir:

- Cache semantics: prefix/KV cache helps when the prefix is stable between requests (e.g., system prompt, user profile snippets). If PulseMed's flows have highly dynamic prompting (free-text user history each turn) the hit-rate can be much lower than 40%. Recommend adding a simple instrumentation gating step in the pilot to measure real hit-rate at 1k users for 72 hours.
- Batching trade-offs: continuous batching works best when request arrival has microbursts. For steady low QPS with tight latency SLOs (<200ms) batching gives less benefit. For the pilot, suggest enabling a conservative batching window (25ms) with a low max-batch-size so we can capture throughput gains without large tail latency increases.
- Model variant fallback: our MAP should include a fallback to a slightly smaller quantized variant for non-critical routes to control spend during burst periods. That should be a line item in the MAP under 'cost controls'.

I'll push a short monitoring checklist for the pilot (prefetch hit-rate, mean latency pre/post-batching, tokens/day) into the Drive link.

— Karthik
